title: Egg sandwich on white bread with meat and cheese

content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich with meat and cheese on white bread is a classic breakfast or light lunch. It consists of two slices of soft white bread, a fried egg, a slice of cooked or smoked meat (such as ham or bacon), and a meltable cheese that softens from the heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg sandwiches have been popular in the US and UK for over a century.
White bread is often used for its soft texture that holds the filling well.
The combination of egg, meat and cheese provides a complete set of proteins, fats and some B‑vitamins.
Variations with added vegetables (tomato, spinach) make the dish more balanced.
Thermal processing of the meat and egg makes the sandwich safe to digest.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat are complete protein sources essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B6 and B12 vitamins in the egg and meat support energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Carbohydrates from the bread combined with fats from cheese and meat provide quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Some dietary fiber
items.content: While white bread contains less fiber than whole‑grain varieties, it still contributes a modest amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑dense due to fats in cheese and meat, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and certain meats contain saturated fats, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats and cheese often contain high salt, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs or milk products should avoid this sandwich.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Toast the bread until lightly golden. Fry the egg (sunny side up or over hard) and the meat (ham, bacon). On the bottom slice place the meat, then the egg, followed by a slice of cheese. Top with the second slice of bread and let the cheese melt slightly. Optionally add sauce or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in food‑grade film. Keep bread and fillings separate when storing to prevent sogginess.
